stages.note: Multicloud gets a role in your account. No access key leaves your laptop. Run every command of this stage in the same terminal and folder.

steps.h: Sign in to Multicloud from the CLI
steps.d: The browser opens. Sign in with the same account as on multicloud.io. You must be the organization owner. If you belong to more than one organization, add --org <organization-id> to every mctl command.
steps.c:
mctl auth login
mctl auth status
steps.g: No browser opens (Windows with WSL, SSH, a container): run mctl auth login --no-browser. It prints a link and a code; open the link in any browser.

steps.h: Make a folder for the connection
steps.d: mctl writes the role definition (multicloud.tf) and the OpenTofu state into this folder. Keep the folder after the PoC: you need it to remove the role later.
steps.c:
mkdir multicloud-aws && cd multicloud-aws
export AWS_PROFILE=poc
export AWS_REGION=us-east-1

steps.d: Replace <account-id> with your 12-digit AWS account ID. The two flags at the end answer two questions for you: do not turn on other AWS regions, and do not file quota requests automatically (you do that in the next stage).
steps.g: The output has a line like: Next: mctl cloud-account apply 7. (The line By hand: … after it is for people who apply without mctl; skip it.) The number (here 7) is your cloud-account ID. It is not your AWS account ID. Write it down: you need it in this stage and when you create the pool. To see it again, run: mctl cloud-account list

steps.h: Create the role in your account
steps.who: You review the plan and type yes
steps.d: Replace <cloud-account-id> with the number from the previous step. OpenTofu shows the IAM role it creates and asks you to confirm. After the apply, mctl waits until Multicloud can use the account.
